description: The species the rule lifts barriers for. Must be a species_code of the bundle's parameters_fresh.csv, whose row is that species' first lift rule (`own`).
The rule's name, unique per species. Not `own`, which names the parameters_fresh row. Evidence rows carry it in barrier_override_evidence.lift_rule.
Which barrier kinds the rule may lift. Only `natural` (gradient, falls, subsurface flow) is accepted until human-made barriers can block a species; any other value is refused at load.

Semicolon-separated observation species codes counting toward this rule's threshold, as in parameters_fresh.csv. Each code counts under the record rule (which codes count as which species, and from what date).
Minimum count of distinct qualifying records upstream of a barrier for this rule alone to lift it. A barrier is lifted where any of a species' rules is met; records of two rules never add together.

Earliest observation_date that counts toward this rule. Under pipeline: observation_record_date: lift_floor it must equal the record floor of every species the rule lists (their parameters_fresh observation_date_min), as the parameters_fresh row's must.
Tolerance in metres passed to fwa_upstream() when testing whether a record lies upstream of a barrier position.
Whether a user_barriers_definite_control row with barrier_ind TRUE vetoes this rule's lift at its position.
When the rule was added or last changed.
Where the rule comes from: a study, bcfishpass's model SQL at a pinned commit, or an issue.
